about: A member's counted hours after a reset (redesign RD-36; the owner, 15 Nov: one member, everywhere). A super admin resets one member's hours; from that moment they count from zero on the TV's hours leaderboard, for a play-time Bonus and in the total on the Members list. Time played before the reset counts for nothing. A stint that began before it and ended after counts for the share of its played time that came after, in proportion to the clock, rounded down to the second: time away is not known by the minute, so each part of the stint bears its share. Moments are ISO times; 'never' is a member whose hours were never reset. Proved against @rivr/domain countedSeconds and private.counted_seconds.

cases.description: Never reset: three hours at the table with twenty minutes away count whole, 160 minutes.
Reset before the stint began: it counts whole.
Reset at the very second the stint began: it counts whole.
Reset after the stint ended: none of it counts.
Reset at the very second the stint ended: none of it counts.
Reset two hours into a three-hour stint with no time away: the last hour counts.
Reset two hours into a three-hour stint with twenty minutes away: a third of the 160 minutes played, 53 minutes 20 seconds.
A share that is no whole second is rounded down: 1,000 seconds of a 3,000-second stint with 2,000 played is 666.67, so 666.
Reset one second before the stint ended: one second of the clock, a share of 0.99 of a second played, counts for nothing.
A stint with nothing played, all of it away, counts for nothing either side of the reset.
